docs.title: AKS SRE Platform — evidence, not a live cluster
docs.text:
Current state (2026-10-21): aks-portfolio-dev and its resource group were deleted after a transient Azure validation run. The AKS evidence below is historical; the local kind environment is a separate dry-run profile. See the teardown record and engineering checkpoint.

This project addresses a platform team's need to review infrastructure changes, reject invalid manifests before deployment, and say precisely which runtime claims have been measured. The reference workload is deliberately small; its /sync route is a no-op, not an enterprise inventory integration.

Capability Evidence level Source AKS node placement, private ACR pull by digest, federated Workload Identity token exchange Historical Azure validation, cluster deleted AKS run · identity Argo CD reconciliation, Gateway API/Envoy, Prometheus/Grafana alert cycle Local kind only architecture HPA/Cluster Autoscaler, NetworkPolicy deny, PDB/drain, 30-day SLO, DR Not verified claim matrix

docs.title: Delivery path
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  A[Reviewed Git change] --> B[CI: Terraform, render, policy, ownership]
  B --> C[Canonical GitOps source]
  C --> D[Argo CD on local kind: measured]
  D --> E[Reference workload]
  E --> F[Local metrics and alert proof]
  B -. invalid change rejected .-> A

The GitOps, Gateway and observability nodes in this diagram were tested on kind, not AKS. A fresh AKS run would need a saved reviewed Terraform plan, explicit owner approval, runtime probes, and teardown under the repository's cost-safety rules.

docs.title: Four-repository portfolio
docs.text: This site owns the AKS-SRE-Platform claims. The other products have their own code and evidence: OpsBridge, QuanLyKho, and SmartDocumentChatbot. Their current deployment or test status must be checked in those repositories; the existence of a public demo URL does not establish a healthy business API. The portfolio interview index maps the cross-project narrative and its limits.

docs.title: Four-project portfolio — interview map
docs.text:
Each product addresses a separate business problem. These are the paths to the owning evidence; this AKS site does not certify another repo's current deployment, CI, test count, or security scan.

Product Business question Evidence boundary OpsBridge Can flash-sale orders avoid oversell and can operations reconcile asynchronous events? Concurrency, Saga, outbox/inbox and operational review live in its own repository. QuanLyKho Can a tea shop control lot/expiry inventory and require a different human checker before posting? FastAPI/PostgreSQL are business authority; AI is advisory. SmartDocumentChatbot Can a user ask questions over owned documents with citations and a safe refusal? The live RAG path and experimental agent path require separate verification. AKS-SRE-Platform Can a team review platform changes and prove what ran on Azure versus local kind? Historical transient AKS evidence, local GitOps/observability proof, explicit non-claims.

docs.title: AKS/SRE claim to defend
docs.text:
The platform validated node placement, ACR digest pull and token exchange on transient AKS, then deleted the cluster. GitOps reconciliation, Gateway API and alert fire/resolve were measured on local kind. Autoscaler, enforced NetworkPolicy, DR and production SLO history remain unverified.

See the cross-repository interview guide and AKS claim matrix.

docs.title: Architecture and verification boundary
docs.text:
flowchart LR
  PR[Git PR] --> CI[Offline Terraform and manifest gates]
  CI --> TF[AKS foundation: transient Azure validation]
  CI --> GIT[GitOps manifests]
  GIT --> ARGO[Argo CD: local kind proof]
  ARGO --> WORK[FlashSale and LegacyApp reference workloads]
  WORK --> OBS[Prometheus/Grafana: local kind proof]
  TF -. target, not measured together .-> ARGO

The AKS cluster was deleted on 2026-10-21. Its historical Azure evidence covers system/user pool isolation, private ACR pull by digest, and a scoped Workload Identity token exchange. It does not prove that Argo CD, Envoy Gateway or Prometheus/Grafana ran on AKS. Those components were exercised on local kind.

docs.title: Ownership and trade-offs
docs.text: Decision Business reason Trade-off / measured boundary Terraform provisions platform infrastructure; application repositories own their workload contracts Keep cloud boundary and workload release authority separate Cross-repo source and destination must be validated before Argo sync GitOps reconciles declarative workload state Detect drift and give a reviewed rollback path Kind self-heal measured at 21 s for spec drift and 17 s to recreate a deleted Deployment; Azure runtime not measured System pool separated from user pool Protect critical AKS components from tenant scheduling Placement proven in transient Azure run; autoscaler scale-out not proven Workload Identity plus kubelet-managed ACR access Avoid static Azure credentials in the tested paths Pod token exchange and kubelet image pull are distinct identities; no general claim about every workload Azure-first proof with transient cluster Demonstrate Azure-only behavior within 10-vCPU quota Cluster is deleted after validation; no production uptime/SLO history

docs.title: Failure paths to explain
docs.text:
1. A malformed or unowned manifest fails CI before a deployment claim.
  2. Manual spec drift or a deleted Argo-owned Deployment is detected and reconciled on kind; evidence names the exact context and timing.
  3. A missing Azure-specific proof stays not verified. Applying a NetworkPolicy object is not evidence that unwanted traffic was blocked.
  4. A failed deployment uses a reviewed Git revert as the desired-state rollback; a live AKS rollback is not claimed in this repository.

Read the audit matrix, ADR-014, and current state.

docs.title: Historical AKS validation — cluster deleted
docs.text:
Evidence status: AZURE_K8S_LIVE_VERIFIED for the historical control-plane observation; AZURE_CLOUD_APPLY_NOT_VERIFIED for Terraform apply because no command output from that apply was committed. These labels describe different claims. The cluster aks-portfolio-dev was deleted on 2026-10-21.

Observation Evidence Limit AKS control plane, one Ready system node at Kubernetes v1.36.4 Read-only Azure re-verification Point-in-time observation; cluster no longer exists System/user pool placement, private ACR digest pull, scoped Workload Identity token exchange Phase 7A final report Earlier transient run; proof identities/pools were deleted Saved Terraform plan Plan artifact Does not establish that apply command ran Teardown Runbook execution transcript Historical completion, not a live resource check today

No Argo CD, Gateway API, Prometheus/Grafana runtime, autoscaler scale-out, NetworkPolicy deny probe, or production SLO history is proven by this Azure run. The local architecture page names the separate kind proof.

docs.title: Reproducible checks and their limits
docs.text:
The numbers below are from this repository only. Other portfolio projects must be checked at their own commit; this page does not reproduce their test output or aggregate their vulnerability scans.

Check Result at Current HEAD Reproduce Gate regression script (G1–G14) 47 assertions passed, 0 failed .venv/bin/python tests/test_gates.py Terraform configuration validation Success! Configuration is valid (0 syntax/provider errors) terraform -chdir=terraform/aks-foundation validate Envoy Gateway kustomize root Rendered successfully; syntax/composition only kubectl kustomize platform/envoy-gateway/gateway >/dev/null LegacyApp reference workload 4 tests passed; /sync is a no-op cd apps/legacy-inventory/src && npm test GitOps validator (Standalone mode) 16 passed / 0 failed / 2 not-present (advisory, NOT_PRESENT never masked) python3 gitops/validate-gitops.py GitOps validator (Multi-repo mapped) 18 passed / 0 failed / 0 not-present (full cross-repo render) python3 gitops/validate-gitops.py --repo-map gitops/repo-map.local.yaml

The gate script is tests/test_gates.py; there is no tests/test_gate_matrix.py in this repository. A green render or unit test does not prove live AKS deployment or operational reliability. For the environment-labelled claim table, see current state and the audit matrix.

docs.title: Workload Identity and private image pull — historical proof
docs.text:
The Phase 7A run proved two different credential paths on real AKS:

  1. A proof pod's Kubernetes ServiceAccount token was exchanged through an Entra federated credential for a scoped Azure Reader operation.
  2. The kubelet managed identity pulled a private ACR image by digest without an imagePullSecret.

The pod did not use its Workload Identity to pull the image. The run did not prove that all workloads use federation, nor that an application pod read a Key Vault secret. The temporary proof identity, pool and AKS cluster were deleted after validation.

Claim Primary evidence Federated token exchange and scoped read Workload Identity runtime report Kubelet ACR pull by digest, no pull secret Private ACR pull report

The demo uses saved, sanitized evidence. Do not run an old kubectl command against an unspecified context: the Azure cluster in that report no longer exists, and the active local context may be kind.

docs.title: FinOps boundary for transient AKS proof
docs.text:
The AKS validation cluster was deleted on 2026-10-21. A monthly estimate for a continuously running cluster would misstate this project's current cost. The recorded 10-vCPU regional quota is a point-in-time capacity measurement, not an Azure invoice or a guarantee that today's quota is unchanged.

The validation design uses one 2-vCPU system node and up to three 2-vCPU user nodes, leaving two vCPU under the measured quota. Autoscaler and full observability are separate experiment profiles under that envelope; they have not been proven together on AKS.

For any future Azure run: remeasure quota and price, review a saved Terraform plan and explicit approval, record start/end and resources, capture runtime proof, then follow the teardown runbook. Budget alerts warn; they do not stop spend automatically. Do not infer actual cost from a VM SKU table without Cost Management data.

docs.title: Incident-response demonstration boundary
docs.text:
The current AKS cluster has been deleted. The repository contains a local kind alert fire/resolve proof, not production incident-response SLOs or contracted P0/P1 response times.

For a local interview walkthrough, use the recorded alert cycle: the metric source became unavailable, LocalPlatformMetricSourceDown fired, the source recovered, and the alert resolved. State the environment, timestamps and what was not measured. The separate self-heal record proves two Argo-owned resource recovery cases on kind.

For a real incident, first identify the exact cluster context and affected service, preserve logs/metrics and timeline, assign an incident owner, and select the owning workload's rollback or repair runbook. A manual kubectl rollout undo against an Argo-managed resource can be overwritten by GitOps; the reviewed Git source must express the intended rollback. Azure commands in the historical teardown runbook are not a routine incident demo.
